plan:
I believe the target is the classical Indian hasta (mudra) where the index and middle fingers are held straight and together, the ring finger is strongly curled into the palm, the little finger is slightly curved inward, and the thumb is swept across the palm touching or near the ring finger base. Orientation: palm faces the camera, fingers pointing up, slightly rotated so the thumb side is angled away from the viewer (small positive yaw). Desired joint placements (starting from zero-open hand):
- Index: mcp ~ 10-20° flex, pip ~ 0-5° (nearly straight), dip ~ 0-5°
- Middle: mcp ~ 10-20° flex, pip ~ 0-5°, dip ~ 0-5° (kept straight and together with index)
- Ring: mcp ~ 80° flex, pip ~ 90° flex, dip ~ 60° flex (strongly clenched into palm)
- Little: mcp ~ 30-45° flex, pip ~ 20-40° flex, dip ~ 10-20° flex (curved inward but not touching)
- Thumb: cmc_flex ~ 30° (sweep across palm), cmc_abd ~ -10° (pressed slightly alongside index side), cmc_rot ~ 0-10°, mcp ~ 20° flex, ip ~ 5-15° flex (thumb tip near ring finger base)
- Finger abductions: index F_abd ~ 0° (close to middle), middle F_abd ~ 0°, ring F_abd ~ 0°, little F_abd ~ -5° (tilted slightly toward ring)
- Whole hand turn: pitch ~ 0-10° (maybe tip slightly toward camera), yaw ~ 10-20° (tilt so thumb side is angled away), roll ~ 0°.
I will implement this gradually respecting max 45° per-call joint change limits. I will first set major flexions for ring and little and initiate thumb sweep and slight hand yaw, then refine with additional adjustments and looks.

The palm faces the viewer; fingers are tipped slightly toward the viewer. Plan: set thumb into mild opposition (thumb_cmc_flex ~ +30°), thumb_mcp/ip modest flex (~20°). Index and middle: mcp ~55–65°, pip ~65–80°, dip ~10–30°; small positive abduction for index toward the thumb (~+5°). Ring and little: strongly flexed (mcp ~75–90°, pip ~80–100°, dip ~35–50°), little with slight negative abduction (toward palm) (~-10°).
